items.description: A historic port city on the Uruguay River, known for its academic tradition and its role in the nation's formation.
facts: Home to the historic Justo José de Urquiza college
Important river port and educational center
Known as the 'Historical City' of Entre Ríos

items.description: The capital of Formosa Province, this subtropical city features a beautiful riverfront and acts as a gateway to the Pilcomayo region.
facts: Located on the banks of the Paraguay River
Known for its modern 'Costanera' promenade
Center for the region's cattle and timber industries

items.description: A bustling border city in Formosa, located across the river from Asunción, Paraguay, and serving as a key trade link.
facts: The second-largest city in Formosa Province
Strategic commercial point on the Paraguay River
Connected to Paraguay via the San Ignacio de Loyola bridge

items.description: The capital of Jujuy Province, nestled in the Andes foothills and serving as the gateway to the stunning Quebrada de Humahuaca.
facts: Known as 'La Tacita de Plata' (The Silver Cup)
Surrounded by colorful mountains and valleys
A major cultural center for Andean traditions

items.description: A productive city in the fertile San Pedro valley, known for its sugar industry and lively carnival traditions.
facts: Center for major sugar cane and citrus production
Famous for its vibrant 'Carnaval de las Yungas'
Located in a lush, subtropical ecological zone

items.description: An industrial city near the capital of Jujuy, historically significant for its steel production and mineral processing.
facts: Known as the 'Industrial Capital' of Jujuy
Site of the first blast furnace in Argentina
Strategic center for the regional mining industry

items.description: The capital of La Pampa Province, Santa Rosa is a tranquil city in the heart of the Argentine pampa, known for its rural heritage.
facts: Founded in 1892 as a rural settlement
Surrounded by vast plains and caldén forests
Home to the impressive Provincial Cultural Center

items.description: The second-largest city in La Pampa, General Pico is a thriving agricultural and industrial hub with a strong pioneering spirit.
facts: Founded at a strategic railway junction in 1905
Major center for soy, corn, and sunflower production
Features a prominent free trade zone

items.description: The capital of La Rioja Province, located at the foot of the Velasco mountains and known for its arid beauty and olive production.
facts: Founded in 1591 by Juan Ramírez de Velasco
Major producer of world-class olives and wines
Gateway to the Talampaya National Park

items.description: The second city of La Rioja, Chilecito is set in a fertile valley famous for its vineyards and historic mining cable car.
facts: Home to the world's longest high-altitude cable car
Renowned for its Torrontés white wine production
Surrounded by the majestic Famatina mountains

items.description: A beautiful desert city transformed by irrigation, Mendoza is the heart of Argentina's wine country and a hub for Andes mountaineering.
facts: World Capital of Wine and Malbec
Gateway to Aconcagua, the highest peak in the Americas
Known for its wide tree-lined avenues and plazas

items.description: Part of the Greater Mendoza metropolitan area, Godoy Cruz is a vibrant city known for its shopping, parks, and historic wineries.
facts: Named after Tomás Godoy Cruz, a local independence hero
Home to the popular San Vicente Park
Significant residential and commercial district of Mendoza

items.description: A historic district in Mendoza, Luján de Cuyo is considered the 'Land of Malbec' and features many of the country's most famous wineries.
facts: The premier region for Malbec grape cultivation
Home to prestigious and historic 'bodegas'
Offers stunning views of the snow-capped Andes

items.description: The capital of Misiones Province, Posadas is a bustling river city acting as a gateway to the Jesuit Missions and the Iberá Wetlands.
facts: Located on the banks of the Paraná River
Connected to Paraguay via the San Roque González bridge
Features a long and scenic riverfront promenade

items.description: A multi-cultural city in Misiones, Oberá was founded by immigrants and is known as the 'National Capital of the Immigrant'.
facts: Hosts the annual National Immigrant's Festival
Surrounded by lush yerba mate and tea plantations
Home to the beautiful Bird Park (Parque de las Aves)
